newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - June 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Queensland Rugby Union officials are likely to push for the final interstate match with New South Wales, scheduled for Saturday week, to be cancelled unless the Australian Rugby Union overturns its decision to prevent Wallaby Test players from participating in the match. Page 20.

Essendon's James Hird will miss the next six weeks of the Australian Football League following scans that revealed an injury he had carried for the first half of the season was a stress fracture of the foot. The Brownlow Medallist was forced from the field last Sunday, adding to Essendon's heavy injury toll that has left them 13th on the premiership ladder. Page 18.

Hunter Mariners fullback Robbie Ross has rejected an offer of A$500,000 over two years to extend his contract with the team. Ross will be free to hold talks with other Super League clubs when his contract with the Mariners expires at the end of this season Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales and Queensland rugby union officials yesterday denied they were targeting Australian Capital Territory Brumbies players after ACT officials said the two sides may try to take some of the Brumbies' best players because they could offer more lucrative contracts. ACT coach Rod Macqueen has asked for more funding so he can keep the team, which reached the Super 12 final this year, together. Page 41.

Penrith won their first Super League match in four games last night after two contentious decisions by referee Brian Grant in the final seven minutes of the game. Penrith defeated Canterbury 28-20, after a controversial penalty was given to Penrith in front of the posts, and a Canterbury try was disallowed due to a scuffle in backplay. Page 41.

Peter Leroy has suddenly resigned after a contentious 13 years in charge of pitch preparation at the Sydney Cricket Ground in order to take up a position in the United States. A team of four ground supervisors including Tom Parker, three-time winner of th Sydney curator of the year award, will now prepare the grounds. Page 42.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League's Melbourne club president, Joseph Gutnick, has declared Melbourne's interim coach Greg Hutchison could have the position on a more permanent basis within the next few weeks. Hutchison was given the position on a temporary basis after the sacking of former coach Neil Balme last week. Page B16.

The Australian Boomers basketball team defeated New Zealand 97-75 in their men's world championship qualifying match last night, after leading by five at half-time. Australia's NBA experienced players Andrew Gaze, Shane Heal and Mark Bradtke stretched their lead late in the match, after a generally close game. Page B15.

Arthur Tunstall has withdrawn as Australia's chief for next year's Commonwealth Games in Kuala Lumpur due to commitments as vice-president of the Oceania Commonwealth Games Federation. Tunstall has been replaced by 1994 Commonwealth Games assistant team manager Don Stockins. Page B15.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian 500cc motorcycle champion Michael Doohan believes his Austrian Grand Prix win at the weekend could be a favourable turning point in his bid for a fourth consecutive title. The win put Doohan 31 championship points ahead of his nearest competito, Alex Criville, and gives him 38 career wins. Page 66.

Victorian seam bowler Peter Reiffel and former Victorian Adam Dale are being considered as possible replacements for Andy Bichel, who is touring with the Australian cricket team in England. Team physiotherapist Errol Alcott will decide in the next two day whether Bichel will be sent home due to his hip injury. Page 66.

Melbourne captain Garry Lyon will meet with coaching staff in the next two days to decide whether he will continue to play, after concerns about his long term back injury. There has been speculation that the injury will require surgery, which would put Lyon out for the rest of the Australian Football League season. Page 69.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Super League club Canberra Raiders are considering sacking star halfback and captain Ricky Stuart at the end of the year. Raiders chief executive Kevin Neil denies Stuart will be sacked, but Stuart claims the decision is all but made. Stuart is under contact to the Raiders for another three years but believes the Raiders are hoping another club will buy the contract. Page 60.

Australian-based boxer Kostya Tszyu is likely to get a chance to regain the IBF Junior Welterweight title that he lost to American Vince Phillips. Talks were held about a possible bout in Sydney later this year. The previously unbeaten boxer will return home tomorrow rather than today after a doctor advised he should rest for another day. Page 59.

Sydney Kings medical staff are confident captain Bruce Bolden could start on the bench in the team's National Basketball League match against the Melbourne Tigers on Saturday, after missing three games due to a hamstring injury. The final decision will be made by the coach Alan Black. Page 55.
